Adds a third instance button next to silent and DND in the HyperOS 4 volume panel so noise cancelling, transparency and off can be switched directly. Expanding the headset menu in the volume panel also lets you disconnect the connected headset.

This module started with a simple idea: a more intuitive and quicker way to switch noise cancelling. If you run into problems, feel free to ask in the group or open an issue on GitHub. If it works well for you, a star is more than enough.
Replay the four step first-run guide
HyperVolumeANC builds on the following open source projects and public interfaces. Thanks to every author and contributor.

Xiaomi and Apple earbuds are supported natively. Sony, Huawei and OPPO headsets are controlled through the interfaces published by their modules; this module does not implement any headset protocol itself.

A quick noise control button for the HyperOS 4 volume panel
Adds one more instance button next to silent and DND so noise cancelling is one tap away
Supports noise cancelling, transparency and off, with an optional three state cycle
Expanding the headset menu in the volume panel lets you disconnect the headset directly
This module and its interface were written together with Codex

1. HyperVolumeANC is a local module that runs on LSPosed. It only changes how the volume panel looks and how headsets are controlled on this device. It only reaches the network to check for updates and never collects or uploads personal data.

2. Enable the module in LSPosed and check the “System UI (com.android.systemui)” and “Bluetooth extension (com.xiaomi.bluetooth)” scopes, otherwise the noise control button will not appear in the volume panel.

3. Xiaomi earbuds and AirPods are supported by the system itself. Sony, Huawei and OPPO headsets rely on third party modules such as SonyPods, HuaweiPods and OppoPods; their licences and terms also apply.

4. This module is provided “as is” without any warranty. Flashing, module conflicts and system updates can all cause problems, so please use it with that in mind.

Module switches and supported headsets live in Home, module status, appearance and app info in Settings, and the credits in About. If the noise control button does not show up in the volume panel, check the scopes and restart the scopes or the phone once. If it works for you, a star on GitHub is much appreciated.
